_note: DEC-2026-014 replaces the misleading total-emitted-JavaScript ceiling with hard runtime-specific shared, largest-asset, and representative-route initial-JavaScript budgets. DEC-2026-015 applies the same reasoning to authored CSS. DEC-2026-017 finishes the CSS half: the enforced ceilings now measure gzipped transfer size, which is what a browser downloads, and carry headroom sized for ordinary styling work rather than for the last build. Uncompressed totals stay visible as trends. Byte values are uncompressed build output unless a name says transfer; user-centric targets remain below.

standalone._note: The whole-artifact ceiling is the real constraint: this file has to open from a disk with no server. Both enforced limits here were pinned within 0.1% of the build that set them -- 3,353 and 1,882 characters -- so any change failed one of them; DEC-2026-017 re-sizes both to targets with room to work under, measured 5,175,243 and 2,259,118. Inlined CSS characters became a trend in the same decision because the inliner turns every url() into a data URL, so about four fifths of that count is base64 fonts and images rather than stylesheet text.

demo._note: C9 stage 4 raised the demo ceilings by 8,045 bytes on 2026-09-05, after removing far more than it added. Connected sign-in, the connected dashboard cards, and the connected proposal record had been reaching the demo bundle: `sideEffects: ["*.css"]` in package.json lets webpack drop the network-only gateway graph the RuntimeProvider references but the static export never calls, the connected auth flow is loaded on demand, and the legacy solver dashboard and proposal list lost their connected branches entirely -- in network mode those routes render ConnectedSolverRoute, so the branches were unreachable code. Together that recovered 137,206 bytes. What remains is the session-aware application chrome and the shared state labels both personas now use, which the static export does render.

network._note: C9 raised the connected route ceilings by 4,153 bytes on 2026-09-05, measured against the build that converted the proposal, team, saved/offer, organization-inbox and notification page families to server authority. The increase is the typed command gateways the RuntimeProvider composes for those nine families; every connected page component itself is loaded on demand and stays out of this chunk. The demo ceilings guard the public static export and were not raised -- they fell by 4,761 bytes in the same change. C9 stage 4 raised them a further 5,260 bytes: the connected sign-in and activation flow, the shared unread-notification hook both shells now use, and the team card the team dashboard was missing. The connected page components themselves are still loaded on demand and stay out of this chunk.

staticAssets._note: Enforced on gzipped transfer size since DEC-2026-017. The uncompressed ceilings these replace had moved 503,436 -> 513,000 -> 516,000 -> 520,000 in a fortnight, each time because ordinary styling work had crossed a line drawn at the previous build; CSS compresses to about a sixth, so they charged every rule roughly six times its cost to a reader. Measured 99,827 total and 39,429 largest when this was set, leaving about a quarter of each for further work. Run `npm run css:prune --check` before raising either; if it reports anything, remove that instead.

source._note: Re-based 2026-09-07 from 625,973 to the tree that carries the solver dashboard, team workspace and sign-in refinements. A trend line that warns permanently is one nobody reads, so this moves when a change deliberately accepts the growth it reports.

webVitals._note: User-centric p75 targets on Persian-market mobile (DEC-2026-009, 95 §7). Not enforced by check:budgets — Lighthouse/RUM evidence is required by the G5 pilot-hardening gate.
